chunks: Al-Saffar from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Zakariyya ibn Yahya al-Kandi al-Raqqi from Dawud al-Raqqi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When the crescent is sought in the East in the morning and is not seen, then it is here: a new crescent, whether it was seen or not."

key_terms.اَلْمَشْرِقِ: The East, referring to the eastern direction or regions
key_terms.اَلْهِلاَلُ: The lunar crescent, used to determine the start of lunar months
key_terms.غُدْوَةً: In the morning, specifically at dawn
key_terms.هِلاَلٌ جَدِيدٌ: A new crescent, indicating the beginning of a new lunar month

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if the lunar crescent is not seen in the east at dawn?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the rule for the new moon's visibility: if it is sought in the eastern regions at dawn but not seen, the month is considered to have begun, regardless of actual sighting. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the eastern horizon as the primary reference point for lunar calendar calculations, ensuring uniformity in religious observances. It reflects the practical application of astronomical knowledge within fiqh to determine the start of months like Ramadan and Shawwal.
